claims.claim: Finite-sequence survival with unrotatable dominoes is in NP.
claims.evidence: For a sequence of n explicitly represented pieces, certify one locking position per piece. For each current board, the fixed-orientation piece has only O(WH) legal translation states, including any constant-size spawn buffer required by the rules. Directed reachability from spawn to the certified lock is decidable by graph search; the verifier then checks support, loss conditions, placement, and deterministic full-row deletion. If a legal path exists, a simple path of polynomial length exists. Repeating this n times is polynomial, proving membership in NP.
claims.witness: A certificate consists of n locking coordinates, optionally augmented by simple movement paths, one for each input domino.
claims.search_method: Direct polynomial-verifier proof, supplemented by an exact integer-bitmask implementation of spawn reachability, locking, and simultaneous row deletion.

claims.claim: For row-parallel unrotatable dominoes on an odd-width board, there is a computable linear-size upper bound on the number of pieces that can ever survive.
claims.evidence: Track physical rows as tokens. Until a token clears, each initially occupied cell remains an uncrossable barrier, and every horizontal domino assigned to that token occupies two adjacent cells in one initial empty interval. Thus token i receives at most ci=Σj floor(ℓi,j/2) pieces. Clearing requires a perfect domino tiling of every interval, so it is possible only when every ℓi,j is even; consequently at most q initial tokens clear. Every clear introduces one empty top token. For odd W, that token has a single odd interval and can never clear, while accepting at most floor(W/2) pieces. Hence U=C+q floor(W/2) is a valid bound. Moreover U≤2H floor(W/2)=H(W−1), and C,q,U are obtained by one grid scan. Exact exploration of all 1,640 boards of sizes 3×1, 3×2, 3×3, 5×1, and 5×2 found no cycle and always found the exact maximum at most U.
claims.witness: The explicit bound is U=Σi,j floor(ℓi,j/2)+q floor(W/2), where q counts initial rows whose empty intervals all have even length.
claims.search_method: Row-token invariant proof plus exhaustive exact finite-state search over 1,640 small odd-width boards.

claims.claim: On an even-width board, two initially empty top rows suffice for survival of arbitrarily many row-parallel unrotatable dominoes.
claims.evidence: Pair adjacent columns. With the top two rows empty, the highest occupied cell h in any pair is at most row H−2, so a straight drop into that pair locks no higher than H−1 and leaves row H empty for lateral access. Place once in every pair; absent a clear, both columns of each pair then have the same top. Let T≤H−1 be the largest such top and stack lower pairs to T. An earlier clear restores two empty top rows because the untouched old top row shifts down and a new empty row enters; restart then. If no earlier clear occurs, completing all pair tops fills row T and clears it. Every phase therefore safely produces a clear after finitely many placements and restores the invariant, so iteration survives infinitely. The checker executed six consecutive phases from each of 4,454 eligible small boards, totaling 26,724 verified clears; the largest tested phase used seven pieces.
claims.witness: Repeated strategy: initialize each fixed adjacent-column pair with one straight-dropped domino, level all pair tops to their common maximum, and restart immediately after any premature clear.
claims.search_method: Invariant-and-termination proof, supplemented by exact strategy simulation for widths 2, 4, 6 and heights 2 through 4 where applicable.

claims.claim: The maximum survival length on an initially empty odd-width W×H board is exactly H floor(W/2).
claims.evidence: Starting from empty, every horizontal placement changes one row's occupancy by two. Inductively no odd-width row can become full, so no row clears. Each row contains at most floor(W/2) disjoint dominoes, giving the upper bound. For W≥3, every edge of the odd path on W cells belongs to a maximum matching: after selecting that edge, maximum matchings of the two residual subpaths supply floor(W/2) edges in total. Choose such a matching containing the fixed spawn pair and fill it level-by-level. On the top level, place matching edges farthest-to-nearest on each side and the spawn pair last, leaving the required travel cells unobstructed. One cell remains empty in every row. This locks exactly H floor(W/2) pieces; W=1 is the trivial zero-piece case. Exact search verified both optimum and construction for W=3,5,7 and H=1,2,3,4.
claims.witness: For example, on an empty 5×2 board with spawn columns 2–3, lock pairs 2–3 and 4–5 on the bottom, then 4–5 and finally 2–3 on top, for four surviving pieces.
claims.search_method: Parity upper bound and explicit path-matching construction, checked by exact exhaustive search in 12 small parameter cases.

claims.claim: The row-capacity bound is not sufficient, and clearing one row does not guarantee indefinite unrotatable-domino survival.
claims.evidence: For the 3×3 board top/middle/bottom = .../.#./..., C=2,q=0,U=2. Both horizontal positions contain the middle column, so the central obstruction forces the first piece to lock in the top row; either top placement intersects every width-three spawn pair, making a second placement impossible. The exact maximum is therefore one, disproving sufficiency of U. For the 3×2 board .../..#, a bottom placement in columns 1–2 completes and clears that row. The resulting empty 3×2 board has exact maximum two by the preceding theorem, so the original board survives three pieces but not four despite clearing a row. Here C=2,q=1,U=3. Exact state search reproduced both maxima and the specified clearing move.
claims.witness: Concrete witnesses are the 3×3 board .../.#./... with U=2 but maximum 1, and the 3×2 board .../..# whose bottom-left domino clears a row but whose maximum is only 3.
claims.search_method: Direct obstruction proofs plus exhaustive exact reachability and maximum-length computation for both concrete boards.

target_evidence: The exact target requests a computational-complexity classification for arbitrary finite unrotatable-domino survival instances. The draft establishes the general NP upper bound, but proves neither a polynomial-time algorithm nor NP-hardness/NP-completeness for arbitrary initial boards and sequences. Claims 1–4 concern only the row-parallel subfamily and impose odd/even-width, empty-top-row, empty-board, or concrete-instance restrictions. They are material, correct progress but do not resolve the requested classification. The final writeup explicitly calls the result partial and identifies the missing algorithm or hardness reduction, so claimed_resolution=PARTIAL is accurate and not overstated.

Persisted and ran an integer-bitmask finite-state checker with no floating-point decisions.
